originals.title: Direct and Indirect Influence of Altruistic Behavior in a Social Network
originals.version: Unmodified publisher full-text HTML response body after HTTP decompression; not a PDF facsimile. No markup or text normalization applied.
originals.reading_scope: Main Introduction (including The Current Study), Methods, Results and Discussion read through publisher HTML. Locators particularly inspected: Fig. 1; Methods > Tasks > Public goods game; Methods > Procedure; Results > Did Seed Node contributions affect Node-1 participants?; Results > Did Seed Node contributions affect Node-2 participants?; Fig. 2. Downloaded HTML checked for bibliographic metadata and matching procedural passages. Dataset, Appendix A and underlying cited studies not independently audited; no replication or reanalysis.
limits: Seed and terminal node contributions were computer-generated; the two intermediate nodes were human participants.
The corresponding earlier human contribution was replayed to a later participant without simultaneous participation.
The second partner contribution was predetermined as 10 minus the first partner contribution.
The experiment does not establish actual donor sacrifice, increased net welfare, adaptive recipient-specific concern, or moral necessity.
